Kunal Mukharjee R/o C-33/1, Khasra No. 967/2, 3rd Floor, Jvts Garden, Chhatarpur Extension, New Delhi. .........Defendant. Suit For Permanent & Mandatory Injunction. Date of institution of suit : 03.02.2018 Date of arguments : 27.05.2024 Date of pronouncement of judgment : 29.05.2024 Ex-Parte Judgment 1. Vide this ex-parte judgment, I shall decide the present suit, filed by the plaintiff against the defendant, for permanent & mandatory injunction as well as miscellaneous application bearing no. 104/2018 under Order XXXIX Rule 2A r/w Section 151 CPC r/w Section 10 & 12 of the Contempt of Court Act, filed by the plaintiff against the defendant. CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 1 /16 2.
texts.facts: The relief sought by the plaintiff by way of present suit is reproduced as under: (a) Permanent Injunction with cost in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant, her agents, servants, legal heirs, associates, attorneys, assignees, successors, administrators or any other person on her behalf, thereby restraining them from creating any hindrance and/or obstruction in Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/ 1 the supply of water of the plaintiff's flat on the first floor of the property bearing No. C-33/1A, Khasra No. 967/2, JVTS Garden, Chhatarpur Extension, New Delhi. (b) Mandatory Injunction with cost in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant, her agents, servants, legal heirs, associates, attorneys, assignees, successors, administrators or any other person on her behalf, thereby directing the defendant to remove her locks from the door of the terrace and allow the plaintiff to go on the terrace and have access to her overhead water tank installed on the terrace of the property bearing No. C-33/1A, Khasra No. 967/2, JVTS Garden, Chhatarpur Extension, New Delhi. It is the case of the plaintiff that the defendant is CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 3 /16 harassing the Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/ 2 plaintiff & her family members, on one ground or the other i.e. by causing obstructions to the water supply of the plaintiff's flat, by putting lock on the door of the terrace etc.
texts.arguments: 6. It is further submitted that due to the acts of the defendant, plaintiff has been constrained to arrange water for cooking food, drinking and cleanliness purposes, on day-to-day basis from outside sources, which is causing great harassment to the plaintiff and her family members. It is further submitted that as per the said maintenance agreement, plaintiff has failed to clear the maintenance charges due to which defendant had also issued a CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 5 /16 legal notice dated 16.01.2018 to the plaintiff, demanding the arrears of maintenance to the tune of Rs. 65,500/-. It is further submitted that the suit property is situated in an unregularized area and there is no supply of water by government aided agencies like Delhi Jal Board and it is the defendant, who is arranging the water supply Veena Gupta vs Myna Mukharjee on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162042048/ 3 through water tank as well as other sources with concerned authorities, in lieu of the maintenance agreement duly executed between the parties. It is averred that the defendant has paid all the expenses for getting the pipeline installed in the said building and there is one electric motor, which runs the water throughout the building and gives uninterrupted supply of water to the residents throughout the day. It is further submitted that the water is stored in the overhead tanks as JVTS supplies water only for a limited time period of one hour and it is the defendant, who stores the water in the underground tank situated at the ground floor and the same is stored at the overhead water tank through electric motor. It is submitted that the plaintiff has failed to pay the maintenance charges of about Rs. 2 lacs and the present suit has been filed with a motive to avoid making the payment of said charges. Counsel for the plaintiff has argued that the defendant has been proceeded ex-parte and therefore, case of the plaintiff stands proved by virtue of unchallenged & uncontroverted evidence. He has prayed that the suit of the plaintiff be decreed accordingly. It is alleged by the plaintiff that the CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 8 /16 defendant no.1 has stopped the supply of water to the plaintiff's flat by putting down the valve outside the overhead water tank, installed on the terrace of the building. On the contrary, defendant has claimed that the plaintiff has not paid the maintenance charges as per the maintenance agreement, executed between them in October, 2016. Secondly, she has claimed that the defendant did not provide the details of the expenses incurred towards the maintenance and misused the said money of the plaintiff & therefore, plaintiff did not renew the said maintenance agreement.

9. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed by the Ld.
Predecessor vide order dated 29.07.2019.
Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of permanent injunction as prayed for ?
Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of mandatory injunction as prayed for?
Whether the plaintiff is liable to pay maintenance dues as alleged in the written statement?
Whether the suit is liable to be dismissed on ground of absence of cause of action or locus standi or suppression of material facts?
Though, no evidence has been led by the defendants, however, issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 29.07.2019.

Thus, issue-wise findings of this Court are as under:-
Issue No. 1: Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of permanent injunction as prayed for ?
OPP AND Issue No. 3: Whether the plaintiff is liable to pay maintenance dues as alleged in the written statement?
OPD 15. Issue no.1 & 2. are taken up together as they are intermeshed and discussion on one issue would affect the other issue.

In the instant case, the first relief sought by the plaintiff is to restrain the defendant & her agents, associates etc. from creating any hindrance and/or obstruction in the supply of water of the suit property.
The entire issue, as rightly stated by the defendant in the Written Statement, revolves around the said maintenance agreement, which is admitted by both the parties.

The relevant terms of the maintenance agreement are reproduced as under: -

17. The first assertion of the plaintiff in support of her case is that she has paid the maintenance charges for one year as evident from the receiving given by the defendant on the electricity bill.

With respect to the proof of regular payment of the maintenance charges, plaintiff has merely adduced electricity bill dated 6.04.2017,
which bears the receiving of Rs. 2,157 towards 1/3 rd share of the total bill.
No other document or evidence has been adduced by the plaintiff to show that she has been regularly paying the maintenance charges to the defendant as per the maintenance agreement.
Other than pleading vaguely, the plainti ought to have placed something on record showing that she had been regularly paying the maintenance charges.

Further, the assertion of the plaintiff that the defendant did not provide the details of the expenses incurred towards the maintenance, does not inspire confidence of this court as the defendant has claimed to have sent legal demand notic
The copy of said legal notice, though not been proved by the defendant, has been placed on record and the plaintiff has not denied the same by filing replication.

6 18.

The question that arises at this juncture is whether the plaintiff is entitled to equitable relief of injunction without having proved on record, the payment of maintenance charges as CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 10 /16 per
The law is well settled with regard to the relief of injunction that one who seeks equity must do equity and one who seeks equity must come with clean hands.
If a party is found to be on the wrong side of law by its own acts and omissions, it cannot cry foul.
The Court is duty bound to strictly deal with litigations based on facts, which have either been misrepresented or distorted to suit the convenience of a litigant.

In the case at hand, the maintenance agreement,
executed between the parties is an admitted document and it requires the plaintiff to pay the maintenance charges for availing the services, mentioned therein.

The plaintiff has made contradictory submissions in single breadth by claiming on one hand that she has rescinded from the maintenance agreement and on the other hand that the defendant has not told her the maintenance charges, due & payabl
However, both the submissions lead to the only conclusion that the plaintiff has not paid the maintenance charges as required by the maintenance agreement.

She has further stated that she is still ready to pay the proportionate amount of the electricity charges & the lift services but even her expressed willingness to pay the proportionate amount of the electricity charges & the lift services
Plaintiff herself being in the wrong, is not entitled to claim any equitable relief from the court.
19. Further, plaintiff has asserted that she had signed the maintenance agreement under compelling circumstances and she did not renew it as the defendant was misusing her money.
The CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 11 /16 said assertions are totally baseless & and not supported by any evidence.
Plaintiff has not bothered to explain as to what were the compelling circumstances, which led her to sign the maintenance agreement or how the defendant was misusing the maintenance charges.
Pleading, which is not supported with cogent & substantial evidence is vain.

Another argument of the plaintiff that she had not renewed the said maintenance agreement and therefore, she is not liable to pay the maintenance charges, also does not sustain as the plaintiff admittedly did not forego all the facilities p
Plaintiff can not be permitted under law to accept only some terms of the maintenance agreement and deny the others, as per her own wish unless, there is such clause in the agreement it self.
There is evidently, no such clause in the maintenance agreement.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, it would not be erroneous to hold that the present suit appears to have been filed by the plaintiff to avoid making the payment of the maintenance charges to the defendant as per the maintenance agreemen
Thus issue no.1 & 3 are decided against the plaintiff and in favor of the defendant.
However, it is clarified that this court is not giving any finding on the quantum of maintenance charges to be paid by the plaintiff as the present suit does not call for the same.
Issue no. 2: Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of mandatory injunction as prayed for?
OPP 20.
The relief of mandatory injunction sought by the plaintiff is twofold.

Firstly,
directing the defendant to remove her locks from the door of the terrace and allow the plaintiff to go on the CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 12 /16 terrace & have access to her overhead water tank, installed on the t
Secondly, directing the defendant to immediately restore the supply of water from the overhead water tank installed on the terrace of the property.
21. As far as the second part of the mandatory injunction relief is concerned, it gets declined on the same reasoning and discussion as stated above.

However, as regard the relief, directing the defendant to remove her locks from the door of the terrace and allow the plaintiff to go on the terrace & have access to her overhead water tank,
plaintiff has been able to show through the Agree
The defendant has not disputed the said agreement to sell but claim to have exclusive right to the terrace.
Irrespective of the asserted right/ title of the defendant to the terrace, plaintiff has right to access the terrace for the limited purpose of installation/ maintenance of the water tank.
In view of the same, issue no.2 is partly decided in the favor of the plaintiff and against the defendant.
Issue No. 4: Whether the suit is liable to be dismissed on ground of absence of cause of action or locus standi or suppression of material facts?
OPD 22.
This issue was required to be proved by the defendant.
However, in the absence of any evidence adduced, defendant has CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 13 /16 filed to prove the same.
Thus this issue is decided against the defendant.

By way of application under Order XXXIX Rule 2A, plaintiff has alleged that the defendant has committed the breach of order dated 03.02.2018, passed by the learned Predecessor and therefore, he is liable to be punished as per the law.
Vide ex-parte order dated order dated 03.02.2018, Ld. Predecessor had directed the defendant to restore the water supply of the flat of the plaintiff.

" In view of the fact that the water supply is the basic amenity and it should not be withheld without any just cause, defendant is directed to restore water supply to the flat

It is alleged by the plaintiff that pursuant to the directions given by the Court vide Order dated 03.02.2018, the defendant had restored the water supply of the plaintiff's flat, however, on 30.08.2018, defendant in utter disobedience of t

25. Having gone through the record, I am of the opinion that there is no disobedience of the order dated 03.02.2018 by the defendant as vide the said order, he was only directed to restore CS SCJ- 116/18 Veena Gupta vs. Myna Mukharjee 14 /1

The order restraining the defendant to create any hindrance or obstruction in the water supply to the plaintiff's flat was specifically passed on 29.07.2019.
26.
Moreover, plaintiff has not placed any photograph or adduced any witness on record, in support of the said allegation.

The provision under Order XXXIX Rule 2A CPC has penal consequence &
therefore, it cannot be invoked at the bare & groundless submission of the plaintiff when already they are at logger heads with each other.
To invoke a penal provision, there has to be something more than a bald allegation.
In view of the same, I am of the view that the application under Order XXXIX rule 2A is without any merit and therefore, stands dismissed.

for the purpose of maintenance/install

suit stands dismissed.
